correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation of the actual vector field gives diagonal Jacobian entries \(\beta_1(1-\epsilon\cosh x_1)/5,-1,0,0\). Since \(\cosh x_1\ge1\), the supremum divergence is \(\beta_1(1-\epsilon)/5-1\), yielding the exact boundary and the \(-1/10\) showcase margin. Liouville's determinant formula integrates the time-varying divergence rather than freezing \(\cosh x_1\); Oseledets plus compact support gives the divergence-average Lyapunov sum. The inspected exact checker verifies coefficient reconstruction and the showcase arithmetic.

final_claim: For the displayed four-dimensional hyperbolic-sine flow, the exact divergence is \(D(x_1)=\beta_1(1-\epsilon\cosh x_1)/5-1\), so uniform strict phase-volume contraction holds exactly when \(\beta_1(1-\epsilon)<5\); at \((\beta_1,\epsilon)=(9,1/2)\) the contraction exponent is at most \(-1/10\), and every compactly supported ergodic invariant measure has Lyapunov-exponent sum equal to the stated divergence average.
limitations: Phase-volume contraction only, not existence/boundedness/hyperchaos of an attractor.
